key_insight: Passive syndrome histories can be ambiguous, so extra calibration measurements are needed to safely decide whether an AI-suggested quantum error-correction update will help or harm.
engineering_relevance: The paper provides a certified decision rule for accepting recovery updates under uncertainty and drift, making AI-assisted quantum control safer for deployed error-correction systems.
method: Showed that opposite coherent X rotations can produce identical passive syndrome distributions in an odd-distance toric code.
Used terminal logical measurements on known calibration states to recover the missing sign information.
Built an evaluator that accepts updates only when calibration uncertainty plus a drift bound prove improvement over the current recovery.
evidence_signal: Simulations showed calibration-confidence checks rejected harmful advice while preserving beneficial updates, and a validated channel-specific bound kept more good updates than a general bound under the stated drift assumptions.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on the drift bound and calibration age limits; if drift assumptions are violated, harmful acceptance can occur.
paper_title: Securing quantum error correction against misleading advice from AI agents
